quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What gives a rider the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your whole face if you crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When following a car, position yourself in the center of your lane, directly behind the car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to increase your visibility as a rider?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly. Waving at drivers does not increase visibility.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep riding straight. Slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader, near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead.

questions.question: Who is most likely to crash?

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who lack training and are unfamiliar with their motorcycle.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist scan the road ahead for?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Scan ahead to watch for traffic changes, hazards on the road, and ways to escape danger. Be ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the turn direction.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see what is behind you and spot hazards early.

questions.question: When someone tailgates you, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up makes it more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: Yes, during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Yes, if the rider is comfortable doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multi-lane highway or one-way street. It is illegal.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is helpful when riding through areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This lets more experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding in Oregon?

options.text: Left up to the judge to decide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Severe.
questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict, mandatory penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle to see better when passing on the left?

options.text: In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass on the left. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if you cannot avoid a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery area to keep your balance.
Maintain your speed to improve traction.
Don't worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and slow down as much as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and slow down as much as needed.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery road sections. If you cannot avoid them, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Do not assume they have ridden before and explain what they need to do.
Do not let them ask questions.
Do not explain anything since they are only a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume they have ridden before and explain what they need to do.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle passenger needs to know how to stay safe for both their sake and yours. Never assume a passenger knows what to do. Give them complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: What is the rule when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You can travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish passing within posted speed limits and only in areas where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: At night, should you follow other vehicles at a different distance than during the day?

options.text: Yes, keep a longer distance behind other vehicles at night.
No, keep a shorter distance behind other vehicles at night.
No, always keep the same distance regardless of time of day.
No, following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, keep a longer distance behind other vehicles at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Keep a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: What can you do if your drive chain slips?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tighten the chain
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, try tightening it. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A windshield wiper
questions.explanation: In Minnesota, motorcycles must have a rearview mirror, horn, muffler, one or two headlights, one red taillight, and at least one brake. If the motorcycle has a passenger seat, it must also have footrests or floorboards for the passenger. A windshield wiper is not required.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge at night.
Using high beam headlights always makes it hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlights when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is following you too closely?

options.text: Let the other driver pass you

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things worse by encouraging them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face in a crash
Should not be used with a helmet

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your face in a crash
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and small rocks.

questions.question: What should a passenger do when riding with you?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control and should hold onto passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Limiting how far you ride in one day

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not take artificial stimulants because the effects can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: Is riding at night easier or harder than riding during the day?

options.text: Easier because you can see other vehicles' lights better
Harder because it is difficult to see

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because it is difficult to see
questions.explanation: Night riding is challenging because you cannot see as well as during the day. Without normal shadows and light contrasts, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: How should you help drivers merge onto the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move to the next lane, if possible
Do not worry about it, they need to merge
Ride on the far left shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane, if possible
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if you can.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars collect in the center of the lane. This area is usually safe for motorcyclists to ride on, unless the road is wet. The oily strip is often less than two feet wide. You can ride to one side of it and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Travel to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in the blind spots of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers your intentions.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your lane and shows other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and seem to move more slowly than they really do. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their true location and speed.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases your motorcycle, downshift and slowly move toward it. Once you are close to the dog, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Brake to slow down before shifting safely.
Flash your brakes to alert drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake to slow down before shifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before downshifting, slow your motorcycle to a safe speed. Downshifting too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, brake first to reach a safe speed.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes lane position as conditions change.
Stays in the same lane position at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have three lane position choices. Choose the position that is safest based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If you ride behind a car, you should:

options.text: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
Always ride in the far left part of the lane.
Always ride in the far right part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in a position where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when behind a car. This position makes you most visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that show rules, like speed limits, are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect how well you ride. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your face. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.
